why: Directly reported by the scored run.
statement: p0001's uniform 50-step construction scores R=2/3; since only shape matters, this is the uniform-block baseline.

why: The uniform block is the only construction observed so far and its autoconvolution is triangular.
statement: A single uniform block has a triangular autoconvolution, so its R is exactly 2/3; beating it requires non-uniform heights that make f*f less triangular/more plateau-like.
refuted_if: A single uniform block of any N scores other than 2/3 under the exact knot formula.

why: Only the uniform baseline is known; the two-step idea is a heuristic extrapolation from the triangular-autoconvolution mechanism.
statement: The maximum is above 2/3, and asymmetric multi-level shapes, especially a two-step height ratio near 2:1, are a promising region (possibly around 0.8).
refuted_if: Systematic searches over K=2..4 block shapes and local perturbations find no construction with R above 2/3.

why: p0005 substantially exceeded the 0.8 guess, and the ordering block > smooth > hill-climb is consistent.
statement: Multi-level block shapes are the strongest region found: K=4 equal-width blocks reach R=0.8444 with max/mean height 1.83; more blocks and unequal widths may go higher, while smooth profiles (0.787) and hill-climbing from uniform (0.758) are weaker.

why: Direct measured result.
statement: Optimizing K=4 equal-width block heights with differential evolution reaches R=0.8444, far above the uniform 2/3 and the smooth 0.787.

why: Explains why block shapes beat uniform and smooth profiles.
statement: The block gain comes from making f*f plateau-like: p0005 has 37.7% of knots within 0.1% of the maximum versus 0% for uniform, and its maximum sits at 0.75 of the support.
refuted_if: A construction with a less flat f*f (fewer near-max knots) scores higher than 0.8444.

why: Shows starting point matters; free-form search should start from the block shape instead.
statement: Local hill-climbing from the uniform shape is a weak route: p0006 reached only 0.7583, while direct block optimization reached 0.8444.

why: p0008 confirms more equal-width levels help; p0013 and p0012 show the alternatives tried so far do not beat it.
statement: Multi-level equal-width block shapes are the strongest region found: K=4 reaches 0.8444 (p0005) and K=5 reaches 0.8501 (p0008), while free-width block optimization (p0013) and 8-12-knot splines (p0012, 0.8421) have not exceeded the block best.

why: p0008 scores higher than p0005 with a less flat top, so 'plateau-like' as measured at 0.1% does not explain the gain.
statement: The gain is not from an exact plateau: p0008 (0.8521) has only 24.7% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max (vs p0005's 37.7%) but 40.2% within 1% and 41.5% within 5%, and its max sits at 0.393 of support, so the relevant feature is a broad shoulder near the maximum, not a flat top.

why: Directly shown by p0008's stage lines and its 73% unused budget.
statement: The current best recipe is two-stage: optimize K=5 equal-width block heights (0.8444 -> 0.8501) then fine additive coordinate descent on all N=400 heights (0.8501 -> 0.8521), and it used only 8 s of the 30 s budget.

why: Stage line shows a single 29.9 s stage with no movement; the optimizer never found even the K=5 equal-width gain that p0008 found in 2 s.
statement: Free-width block parametrization (cumulative boundaries + differential evolution, K=5..10, N=400) is a weak search route: p0013 consumed the full 30 s and produced zero gain over equal-width K=4.

why: p0014 was the deliberate challenge and failed to reach the block best.
statement: Multi-level equal-width blocks remain the strongest region: K=6 at N=800 reaches 0.8577 (p0018) while the best smooth/spline family (p0014) tops out at 0.8421 even under a full-budget challenge.

why: the earlier counterexample (p0008 flat but low) is now reversed by the higher-scoring p0018.
statement: Higher R correlates with a broad near-max plateau of f*f: the best shape p0018 has 37.85% of knots within 0.1% of max, above p0017 (33.2%) and p0008 (24.7%), each scoring lower.

why: p0018's stage lines show K=6 gave the whole gain and later stages were zero.
statement: Current best recipe: optimize K=6 equal-width block heights at N=800 (0.8521→0.8577 in 3.6s); the coordinate-refine stage of p0018 never ran because budget was spent on useless K=7–12 stages, so polishing the K=6 N=800 shape is the immediate headroom.

why: stage lines K=7..10 all show before==after.
statement: At N=800, equal-width block optimization saturates at K=6: K=7,8,9,10 each produced exactly zero gain over the K=6 shape in p0018.

why: K=7–12 warm-started from K=6 gave zero, but other seeds were not tried.
statement: For equal-width blocks at N=800 the K=6 shape is a local optimum in K, so further gains must come from coordinate/gradient polish or higher resolution, not more blocks.
refuted_if: A K≥7 equal-width block shape at N=800, seeded differently, beats the K=6 score 0.8577.
An N=800 K>=7 or differently seeded block shape with the same polish beats 0.8585.

text: The problem remains dominated by equal-width block shapes, especially K=6 at N=800. The best recipe is block-height optimization followed by coordinate and analytic-gradient polish, reaching 0.857813 (p0020). K=7-12 stages and free-width searches have not paid, and the N=800 K=6 shape now looks locally saturated. The open questions are whether higher resolution (N=1600/3200) preserves or increases the gain, whether multigrid beats direct upsampling, whether p0017's basin can compete, and whether a genuinely non-block high-resolution construction can escape the block plateau.

why: The stage lines isolate the N=1600 L-BFGS-B as the sole productive step and quantify how weak the alternatives are.
statement: Best recipe: K=6 equal-width blocks at N=800 (0.8577) → upsample to N=1600 → analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B (+9.6e-5, p0020). K≥7 block stages at N=1600 add exactly zero (p0020 K=6..10 all 0), so they are dead weight; coordinate descent adds only ~2e-5 (p0022).

why: p0020 repeats the K=6..10 sweep at N=1600 with identical zero gains.
statement: Equal-width block optimization saturates at K=6 at both N=800 and N=1600: K=7..10 gave exactly zero gain over the K=6 shape in p0018 and again in p0020.

why: The two new results keep the ordering: more near-max knots tracks higher R.
statement: Higher R correlates with a broad near-max f*f plateau: p0022 (38.66% near-max, 0.857740) > p0024 (27.98% near-max, 0.857008) > p0017 (33.2%, 0.852416).

why: Every recent gain is <1e-4 and block/basin variations converge to ~0.8577-0.8578; held only tentatively.
statement: The block-staircase family is near a true ceiling: remaining headroom above 0.858 is small (<0.005) and comes only from resolution scaling plus gradient polish, not from new block counts or basins.
refuted_if: Any construction reaches R>0.862, or a from-scratch non-block profile beats 0.8578.
